title: FanStreamium
tagline: FanStreamium: Decentralizing video streaming inspired by OnlyFans. Utilizing React, Next.js, Lighthouse, Livepeer, RainbowKit, NFTs. Featuring an integrated CMS, Tableland Web3 DB, and Lit Protocol for data control and privacy.
description:
FanStreamium is a revolutionary step in the world of content creation and sharing. At its core, it is a decentralized video streaming platform powered by an amalgamation of technologies such as React, Next.js, Lighthouse, Livepeer, and RainbowKit. The project brings a fresh perspective to the concept popularized by Web2 platforms like OnlyFans, allowing creators to upload videos and set them as public for general access or private for exclusive access to NFT holders.

What sets FanStreamium apart is its two-tier system, namely fs-stream and fs-CMS. While fs-stream provides the user-facing frontend, fs-CMS serves as the robust backend management system. This backend integrates with Tableland Web3 DB to store all data, including user activities and transactions. The use of Lit Protocol allows for intricate permission settings for each data table, ensuring data privacy and control are at the forefront.
how_its_made:
FanStreamium's foundation is built on React and Next.js, bringing together the power of modern JavaScript libraries and server-side rendering. Lighthouse facilitates decentralized video storage, and Livepeer ensures seamless video playback. The wallet connectivity is managed by RainbowKit, enabling secure transactions.

The core innovation lies in the system's integration with Tableland Web3 DB via fs-CMS for storing and managing all data. Lit Protocol plays a crucial role in setting up data table permissions, providing a robust and secure management system. The unique blend of these technologies gives birth to a platform that is not just user-friendly, but also safe, secure, and in sync with Web3 standards. The incorporation of NFTs to grant access to private content paves the way for a more direct and fair monetization model for creators.
